title: Paul McCartney pitches Cold Cuts to Capitol Records | 1974
content:
Paul and Linda McCartney attended a meeting with Capitol Records executives on 9 April 1974.

The McCartneys were guests of honour at the meeting, held at Capitol Tower in Los Angeles. The execs, which included Capitol’s COO Brown Meggs, marketing vice president Don Zimmermann, and promotions executive Al Coury, presented them with a platinum disc for sales of more than one million copies of Band On The Run.

Wings were, at the time, without a drummer, which stymied Paul’s desire to tour. During the meeting he pitched the idea for a cut-price collection of non-album tracks, studio outtakes, and live recordings, to be known as Hot Hitz And Kold Kutz.

Capitol’s people were not sold on the idea. They wanted to capitalise on the success of Band On The Run, and failed to see the benefit of releasing a cheaper follow-up album.

The project originally started out as Hot Hitz And Kold Kutz, with two k’s and two z’s, but then someone at the record company said “Why have cold cuts on a hot hits album?” as a result of which it became simply Cold Cuts. So it went on the back-burner and cooled off, to mix a few metaphors, and then went even cooler when I discovered that it had become a bootleg.

I still have a lovely unused cover the for the album, drawn for me by Saul Steinberg, best known by the public for his New Yorker drawings. I got to know him and for many years was asking him to draw me a cover, and eventually he came up with something. This is probably the most compelling reason to issue the album, actually: just to use his cover!

Paul McCartney
Club Sandwich, Winter 1994

Despite their lack of enthusiasm, Capitol assigned Cold Cuts the catalogue number 3419, and tentatively scheduled it for release in November 1974.

McCartney eventually shelved the project, although he spoke sporadically in subsequent years about reviving and releasing it.

The original idea was based around a title I came up with and quite liked which was Hot Hitz and Cold Cuts. I thought it would be great, you just put all your top hits on it and then some ‘cold cuts’. But actually when I mentioned it to my record label at the time, they didn’t like the idea of the cold cuts, they wanted everything to be hits, hits, hits! So they didn’t particularly go for that idea. But what has happened over the years is many of those cold cuts – which are B-sides and unknown tracks – have been released in our remastered Archive Collection series…

Maybe one day it would make an album. The funny thing is, I was friends with an American artist that I admire a lot called Saul Steinberg. I asked him if he would do a cover for it and he did. It’s a nice thing! So, I’ve got the cover and maybe one of these days it will get released. The thing is, how much can you release without it looking stupid, you know? New album, Archive Collection reissues, and then The Beatles stuff! So, it’s hard to slot in another thing, but maybe one of these days. It would be an interesting little thing!

Paul McCartney
paulmccartney.com, 30 August 2019
